name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: AASLD Guidelines for Diagnosis of PSC

criteria.description: Cholestatic biochemistry (elevated ALP, GGT) for >6 months
Characteristic cholangiographic findings: multifocal strictures and segmental dilatations of intrahepatic and/or extrahepatic bile ducts (beaded appearance) on MRCP or ERCP
Liver biopsy showing periductal (onion-skin) fibrosis (in small duct PSC or when cholangiography is normal)
Exclusion of secondary causes of sclerosing cholangitis (IgG4-related, ischemic, infectious)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Cholestatic biochemistry plus characteristic cholangiographic findings, after exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Small duct PSC has normal cholangiography and is diagnosed by liver biopsy. Up to 80% of PSC patients have concurrent IBD (usually ulcerative colitis).

pathognomonic.notes: Alternating strictures and dilatations of intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts

rare.notes: Lifetime risk 10-15%; major concern; difficult to detect early

laboratory: Elevated IgG4 in ~10% (does not necessarily mean IgG4-related disease)
CA 19-9 elevated (raises concern for cholangiocarcinoma if markedly elevated)
imaging: MRCP: multifocal strictures and dilatations of bile ducts (beaded appearance); gold standard imaging
ERCP: similar findings; allows for therapeutic intervention (balloon dilation, stenting, brushings)
Ultrasound: bile duct wall thickening, gallbladder polyps
CT: periportal lymphadenopathy, heterogeneous liver enhancement
genetic: Strong association with IBD susceptibility loci (IL2RA, MST1)
other: Liver biopsy: periductal concentric fibrosis (onion-skin fibrosis), bile duct proliferation, ductopenia
Colonoscopy: screening for IBD (recommended in all PSC patients even without GI symptoms)
FISH for polysomy/aneuploidy on biliary brushings: screening for cholangiocarcinoma

distinguishingFeatures: Dense IgG4+ plasma cell infiltrate on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive jaundice (concern for dominant stricture or cholangiocarcinoma)
Markedly elevated CA 19-9 (>129 U/mL suggests cholangiocarcinoma)
references: Lindor KD, et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. Am J Gastroenterol. 2015;110(5):646-659.
European Association for the Study of the Liver. EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on sclerosing cholangitis. J Hepatol. 2022;77(3):761-806.
Karlsen TH, et al. Primary sclerosing cholangitis - a comprehensive review. J Hepatol. 2017;67(6):1298-1323.
